title: What base SciBERT produces, and what task training can add
summary: The pinned base SciBERT checkpoint produces contextual token representations and pretrained masked-token predictions. It has no ready-to-use SOFTWARE/VERSION classifier. A trained task head can use SciBERT with either a frozen encoder or further encoder fine-tuning; neither route guarantees accurate extraction without evaluation.

sources.title: AllenAI SciBERT repository and task examples

examples.title: Actual base checkpoint: masked token in software context
examples.input: The microscopy images were analyzed with [MASK] software.
examples.note: Captured offline from the pinned base checkpoint. These are vocabulary-token probabilities at [MASK], not extracted software spans or task-label probabilities.

examples.title: Actual base checkpoint: masked token in clinical context
examples.input: Patients with [MASK] were enrolled in the study.
examples.note: Captured offline from the pinned base checkpoint. The output predicts one masked vocabulary token; it does not identify disease mentions elsewhere in a sentence.

examples.title: Illustrative disease named-entity extraction
examples.input: Participants with asthma received standard care.
examples.note: Desired task-specific output only. This sentence was not run through a disease NER model; a suitable labeled-data-trained head and validation would be needed.

examples.title: Illustrative citation-intent classification
examples.input: We applied the assay introduced by Lee et al. (2020) to quantify the samples.
examples.note: Desired task-specific output only. SciCite has citation-context labels including method; this synthetic sentence was not classified by the base checkpoint.

examples.title: Illustrative PICO extraction
examples.input: Adults with asthma received inhaled budesonide or placebo; symptom scores were measured after 12 weeks.
examples.note: Desired task-specific output only, using a simple teaching schema. The base checkpoint did not produce PICO fields; the SciBERT repository lists PICO as a downstream task.

examples.title: Illustrative scientific relation extraction
examples.input: Compound A inhibited enzyme B in the assay.
examples.note: Desired task-specific output only, with a teaching schema rather than a named dataset label. The base checkpoint did not extract this relation.

evidence.interpretation: The inspected pinned checkpoint contains pretraining heads, with no task classifier weights or software/version label map. This establishes no ready-to-use extraction head; it is not an accuracy test or a claim that every adaptation must update encoder weights.
evidence.probe_scope: Three synthetic inputs, CPU inference, local cached files only, no training or model download.
